newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says agreed intense NATO talks with Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says agreed intense NATO talks with Kohl.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Saturday he had agreed with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl to maintain an "intensive dialogue" on plans, which Moscow opposes, to expand the NATO defence alliance into eastern Europe.
Itar-Tass and Interfax news agencies said Yeltsin told them he agreed during talks with Kohl at his hunting lodge near Moscow "to continue an intensive dialogue at various levels".

"The question is not simple, but I hope that by the European summit in Lisbon in December 1996 we will be able jointly to find a wise solution," he said, referring to a planned summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
An unidentified source told Tass earlier that Kohl had promised that no decisions on NATO enlargement to the east would be taken this year.

Yeltsin, who announced this week he will have heart surgery at the end of the month, added he was "completely satisfied" with the talks with Kohl, a personal friend and the first western leader he has met since his reelection on July 3.
"Our meetings are always marked by warmth and openness and bring concrete results," he said. "This meeting once again showed that Germany is an important partner for Russia."
Interfax quoted unidentified sources as saying that Yeltsin would visit the German spa of Baden-Baden early next year, where he would be presented with a prize by the German press.
The sources also told Interfax that Yeltsin and Kohl agreed to take a break together next year on Lake Baikal in Siberia.
